/ momentic-vs-maestro            Momentic vs  Maestro     YAML is the format. Target resolution is the difference. Momentic resolves natural-language targets, reuses successful interactions, and adds maintenance tools. Maestro flows depend on text and view selectors, with experimental AI checks through Maestro Cloud.             Try for free         Get a demo           Web, iOS and Android · CLI · CI · MCP                        At a  glance.            Compare test authoring, execution, maintenance, and infrastructure.                  Category     Momentic   Maestro           Test artifact    YAML in Git with intent-based and explicit commands    YAML flows in Git with text, ID, and other selectors     Local execution    Momentic CLI and authenticated platform features    Open-source CLI; local core flows without paid Cloud     AI targeting    Cached target signals with AI re-resolution    Selector-based flow commands; separate experimental AI checks     AI assertions    Rubric-based assertions that fail on a failed check    assertWithAI; optional defaults true, set false for a gate     AI service    Momentic manages model execution    AI commands use Maestro Cloud; free account supported     Hosted targets    Chrome variants, iOS simulators, Android emulators    Maestro Cloud target support and local mobile or web flows     Maintenance    Target healing; coding-agent maintenance; triage and repair PRs    Flow changes in Git; AI analysis helps inspect failures     Execution limits    Plan-specific duration and concurrency    Cloud has a 20-minute soft limit per test execution     Diagnostics    Step evidence; coding-agent investigation; classification and triage    Flow logs and artifacts; experimental AI insights reports     Operating model    Commercial runtime and hosted platform    Open-source local CLI with optional Cloud services                       What Maestro does       Maestro provides open-source YAML flows, built-in synchronization, and local mobile and web execution. Maestro Cloud adds hosted runs and experimental AI assertions and analysis. Those AI checks do not replace selector targeting, and an AI assertion is optional by default. Momentic combines natural-language targeting with cached replay and target re-resolution. Exact and AI assertions define the expected outcome, while coding-agent maintenance tools help investigate and repair native tests. Both use reviewable files; the maintenance contract is the distinction.                 Make the semantic check fail on purpose   Both platforms can express a natural-language visual expectation. Evaluate failure semantics and evidence before treating that check as a CI gate.       A localized success screen has the wrong state   Display a localized confirmation after saving a setting, then replace it with an error screen that has a similar layout. The semantic check should distinguish success from failure.         Momentic: a failed assertion fails the test   Use an AI assertion with a precise criterion and known negative examples. Use exact checks for values that do not vary. Model-based assertions run again even when preceding interactions use cached targets. Coding-agent maintenance skills can inspect failure evidence and propose repairs for review.      Maestro: set the required failure behavior   assertWithAI is experimental and defaults optional to true. Set optional: false for a gate. AI commands use Maestro Cloud, including a free account; inspect the generated report as well as the flow status.                   Example    yaml      - assertWithAI:
    assertion: The setting was saved successfully and no error is shown.
    optional: false             Check these in your evaluation   Test correct, incorrect, and ambiguous screens against the same criterion. Check the process exit status and the report when the AI assertion is false. Include managed AI access and model latency in the CI setup. Keep exact values under explicit checks and semantic checks limited to justified criteria.       Documentation       Momentic step caching           Maestro assertWithAI           Maestro AI test analysis                          Why teams  choose Momentic.                 01   Describe the target instead of matching view properties   Momentic commands describe a target in natural language and reuse resolved signals. Maestro tapOn matches text, IDs, or other view properties. Both files are reviewable; when the selector contract changes, a Maestro flow needs a selector update.       02   Wait for application state   Maestro handles common UI readiness rather than requiring a sleep before every command. Momentic also handles interaction waiting. Test a slow screen transition and a background job; application-specific conditions may still need explicit checks or timeouts.       03   Resolve stale targets during execution   Momentic can re-resolve a target when cached signals no longer work. Coding-agent maintenance skills investigate failures and repair tests; triage proposes changes for review. Maestro’s AI analysis examines logs, command metadata, and screenshots to report issues. Diagnosis and run-time target repair are separate mechanisms.       04   Make a failed AI check block the run   Momentic AI assertions fail the test when their check fails. Maestro assertWithAI is experimental and defaults optional to true, so a failed check can let the flow continue. Set optional: false to make it a gate, and test known incorrect screens in either tool.       05   Account for the managed AI dependency   Maestro now routes AI commands through Maestro Cloud and supports a free account; external AI keys are no longer required. Its local core remains a different dependency profile from those AI commands. Momentic’s model execution is also a managed service, so include that dependency in offline or network-restricted requirements.       06   Use the actual native target   Momentic hosts iOS simulators and Android emulators and supports local targets. Maestro’s local and Cloud configurations have their own device requirements. Validate app installation, permissions, deep links, and any system interactions on the configuration you will run in CI.       07   Keep long runs diagnosable   Maestro Cloud documents a 20-minute soft limit per test execution. Momentic limits vary by plan and target. Break long journeys into isolated, diagnosable tests where possible, and confirm cleanup and artifact delivery when a run times out.       08   Get maintenance tools beyond the local runner   Maestro’s open-source local runner supports selector-based flows. Momentic adds intent resolution, hosted execution, and coding-agent maintenance tools around repository tests. Keep the local OSS runner where those additions do not address a recurring cost.                     YAML flows and other  mobile testing  options           The file extension does not define the maintenance burden. Momentic resolves natural-language targets and records cache behavior. Selector-based flows still need updates when their selector contract changes.                Tool   Authoring   Runs on   Best fit           Momentic   YAML in Git; editor and coding-agent tools   Chrome variants, iOS simulators, Android emulators   Intent-based regression tests with managed execution and failure workflows     Maestro   YAML flows with selectors; experimental managed AI checks   Local mobile and web flows; hosted Maestro Cloud targets   Open-source local UI flows with optional hosted execution and AI analysis     Appium   WebDriver clients, platform drivers, and optional plugins   Real and virtual mobile devices; other driver-specific platforms   Native control, physical devices, and extensible language-specific test stacks     MobileBoost (GPT Driver)   Natural-language mobile flows or generated XCUITest and Espresso code   iOS and Android; native code augmented by an SDK fallback   Mobile teams wanting PR-aware code generation or GPT Driver workflows     Autosana   Plain-language flows; code-managed files and agent tooling   Browser and native mobile workflows; verify required target configuration   Repository synchronization, working-copy runs, and shared application context     BrowserStack   Framework suites or Low Code Automation and AI authoring   Broad browser and OS matrix; real iOS and Android devices   Existing automation needing hosted compatibility coverage or physical devices     Sofy   Natural-language agents and platform test workflows   Web, API, and native or hybrid mobile on real devices   Teams evaluating AI-assisted tests alongside hosted physical-device coverage     Tricentis Testim Mobile   Low-code mobile recording and Tricentis test workflows   Native and hybrid mobile through Testim’s current mobile offering   Mobile teams evaluating the current Tricentis platform and migration requirements     mabl   Trainer, reusable flows, and agentic test authoring   Web browsers, native mobile, API, accessibility, performance   Teams choosing a workspace workflow and multiple test types in one platform     testRigor   Natural-language test steps and AI-assisted generation   Web, native and hybrid mobile, desktop, API capabilities   Teams evaluating plain-language authoring and broad application scope                      Who should choose  which.                Choose Momentic   Choose Momentic when UI changes require more than selector edits. Intent-based target resolution, cached replay, and integrated maintenance tools support functional tests across web and virtual native targets.     Try for free               Choose Maestro   Use Maestro for selector-based YAML with an open-source local runner. Its managed AI checks are experimental and require explicit failure settings when used as a release gate. Staff AI Engineer, Mutiny               Browse all                       Related comparisons     Momentic vs Appium       Momentic vs MobileBoost       Momentic vs in-house                          Frequently asked  questions.             Does Momentic run on physical devices?        Momentic’s native targets are hosted or local iOS simulators and Android emulators. Retain a physical-device layer when hardware, OEM behavior, or device-specific performance is required.        What language do I write Momentic tests in?        Momentic uses YAML with intent-based commands, exact checks, and AI assertions. Native setup, builds, accounts, and target-specific commands still need configuration. Maestro YAML follows a different schema and runtime.        Can I run Momentic tests in CI?        Yes. Momentic’s CLI supports CI execution and result reporting. Test the actual build, authentication, target access, and failure policy. Maestro also has local CLI and hosted Cloud workflows with their own limits.        What happens when a resource ID is renamed?        Momentic can re-resolve the intended control when cached target signals no longer match. A missing or ambiguous control can still fail. Current-run resolution does not edit the test. For file changes, use coding-agent maintenance skills or triage and review the proposed diff.        Do AI assertions fail the test?        Momentic AI assertions fail when their check fails. Maestro’s experimental assertWithAI defaults optional to true; set optional: false when failure must stop the flow. Evaluate known positive and negative examples in both.        Is Maestro YAML the same as Momentic YAML?        Both are files that can live in Git, but their schemas and runtimes differ. Maestro flows use its commands and selectors; Momentic uses its own format with intent-based targeting, exact checks, and AI assertions. Migrating requires preserving the outcome in a new executable format.        Does Maestro require my own model API key?        Its current documentation says AI commands are managed through Maestro Cloud, with a free Cloud account sufficient for AI features. External AI provider keys are no longer required. Hosted test execution is a separate Cloud plan requirement.        Will a failed Maestro AI assertion fail CI?        assertWithAI defaults optional to true because the feature is experimental. Set optional: false when failure must stop the test. Inspect the generated AI report and test both correct and incorrect examples before treating the assertion as a release gate.        Can Maestro run without SaaS?        Local core Maestro flows can run with the open-source CLI. Cloud execution and managed AI commands add service dependencies. Momentic’s runtime uses authenticated platform features, so consider that distinction for offline or restricted environments.        What should I compare in a trial?        Run the same mobile flow with stable selectors, a changed layout, and a broken business outcome. Compare cold and repeat timings, selected targets, assertion behavior, reports, and any required repository repair. Include your actual CI device and duration constraints.
